verdicts.reason: Optional chaining short-circuits the whole chain, not just the next access: `groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)` evaluates to `undefined` when `at(0)` is undefined. Verified with node: `({data:{groups:[]}}).data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(x=>x)` returns undefined, and React renders `undefined` as nothing.

Both action arrays are inline literals recreated on every render, and `useRulerRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` list `actions` in their `useMemo` deps, so the memo recomputes every render. The recomputation is cheap (`actions.map`), hence Low.
`.map()` is never reached when `at(0)` is nullish — optional chaining short-circuits the remainder of the chain. There is no runtime crash; the expression is `undefined` and renders nothing.

I reproduced the type in tsc: the union is not discriminated, so after destructuring inside the component `rule ?? promRule` is still `... | undefined` and the code must (and does) fall back to `getEditableIdentifier` returning undefined + `logWarning`. Worse, `promRule` being a *cloud* prom rule satisfies the type but yields no identifier, so the component silently returns null and the whole actions column disappears.

They are compatible. `Alert` is structurally identical to the inline element type of `PromAlertingRuleDTO.alerts`, `RuleHealth` is `string`, and every other member lines up; I compiled the exact shape with tsc --strict and got no error.

The new GrafanaGroupLoader test even asserts the Silence item is present, so the click path is reachable and dead.

The factual regression is verifiable even if the product intent isn't stated anywhere in the diff.
The premise is wrong: optional chaining does not 'only apply to the .rules access' — `a?.b.c()` short-circuits the entire chain when `a` is nullish. No crash is possible from empty `groups` here.
The doc block still reads 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints' while `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` was removed and only `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery` remains.

`key` is still destructured at line 152 and passed to the `datasource` and `default` branches, but the new `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` in the `grafana` branch has no `key`. Mixing keyed and unkeyed siblings in the same mapped array triggers React's key warning and breaks reconciliation as this infinite-scroll list grows.

`canPause`/`canDelete` are OR-ed across both ability sources, but the JSX still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and `rulerRule &&` respectively, so the Grafana-prom half of the OR can never surface a menu item.
Same defect narrowed to Delete: `canDelete` can be true from `grafanaDeleteAbility` alone, but `{canDelete && rulerRule && …}` gates rendering on a ruler rule that promRule-only consumers never pass.

With `skipToken` the hook runs `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`: `loading` is false (useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns early), `isPluginProvided` is false (getRulePluginOrigin returns undefined for undefined), so `duplicateSupported` is `AlwaysSupported` and Duplicate becomes `[true, ctx.hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]` against the *grafana* permission set. Every other ability collapses to false, but Duplicate has no `rulerRule` gate in the menu, so it leaks onto cloud/datasource rules whose own ruler ability says no.

The only non-happy paths are `isPromResponseLoading` (skeletons) and `!promResponse` (error Alert). A successful response with `groups: []` falls through to `at(0)?.rules.map` which yields undefined, so the group renders as a blank region with no message.
